record.paper_title: Some Open Problems on Multiple Ergodic Averages
record.original_question: Let P = {p1, ..., pℓ} be a family of essentially distinct integer polynomials, and let d_min(P) be the smallest integer d such that the Host-Kra factor Z_d is characteristic for mean convergence of the averages (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N T^{p1(n)}f1 · ... · T^{pℓ(n)}fℓ for every system. Is d_min(P) always at most |P| - 1 whenever |P| ≥ 2?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu,T)$ be an invertible measure-preserving system on a probability space. For an integer-valued polynomial $p$, let $T^{p(n)}$ denote the $p(n)$-th iterate of $T$. A family $P=\{p_1,\dots,p_\ell\}$ of integer polynomials is called essentially distinct if $p_i \not\equiv p_j$ for $i\ne j$ and no $p_i$ is constant.

For each integer $d\ge 0$, let $Z_d=Z_d(X,T)$ denote the $d$-th Host–Kra factor of $(X,T)$ (the inverse limit of $d$-step nilfactors when the system is ergodic, with $Z_0$ being the trivial factor). A factor $Z$ is said to be characteristic for the family $P$ (for mean convergence) if for every system $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu,T)$ and all $f_1,\dots,f_\ell\in L^\infty(\mu)$, 
$$\lim_{N\to\infty}\left\|\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^N \prod_{i=1}^\ell T^{p_i(n)}f_i \;-\; \frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^N \prod_{i=1}^\ell T^{p_i(n)}\mathbb{E}(f_i\mid Z)\right\|_{L^2(\mu)}=0.$$
Define $d_{\min}(P)$ to be the smallest integer $d\ge 0$ such that $Z_d$ is characteristic for $P$.

Problem. Prove or disprove: for every essentially distinct family $P$ of integer polynomials with $|P|\ge 2$, one has
$$d_{\min}(P)\le |P|-1.$$
artifact.category_tag: Multiple ergodic averages and Host–Kra factors
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in Frantzikinakis's list of open problems on multiple ergodic averages. Searches did not turn up a published resolution; known results address particular families (e.g., three polynomials, linear forms) but not the general bound $d_{\min}(P)\le |P|-1$. Status appears to remain open.
